top_choice_rationale: The optical lattice clock (Katori and Ye) is a distinct, mature invention: the magic-wavelength condition lets many neutral atoms be interrogated at once without trapping-light shifts, taking optical clocks to about 1e-18 and reproduced across Sr, Yb and Hg. It is separable from the 2005 comb and 2012 single-system control prizes if the citation stays on the lattice concept. Credit to the two names is a defensible judgment on decisive contribution, and a prize is better than none.
